steps.title: Secrets Hub in the Privilege console
steps.what: An admin adds a hub in the Privilege console (Secrets Hub, Add Hubs, Integrate on the GCP card), names it, chooses an account type (Project, Organization or Folder; the guide recommends Project), and pastes a Google service account key.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.

steps.title: Google Cloud Secret Manager
steps.what: The guide says the Secret Manager Admin role is required and the Cloud Resource Manager API must be enabled or sync shows 0 secrets.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.

steps.title: Google service account key with Secret Manage…
steps.what: A secret's value is fetched from Google only when an admin clicks View, using the hub's service account.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.

steps.title: Privilege secret access policy
steps.what: Access is defined with the hub's Policy button: pick a secret, choose Read or Write, name users or groups, and set an expiry.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.

steps.title: Hub Access Summary tab
steps.what: The Access Summary tab lists policies with secret, permission, users and expiry.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.

steps.title: Privilege console audit feed
steps.what: The pasted key was observed once in clear text on the saved hub record in the console audit feed.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.

steps.title: Five providers
steps.what: The Ping deck (Secret Store Management) lists five providers: AWS Secrets Manager, GCP Secret Manager, Azure Key Vault, Delinea Secret Server and CyberArk PAM.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.

steps.title: Nightly re-synchronisation
steps.what: Access runs through the same policy engine as the rest of the platform: read and write are separate grantable actions, every secret read and every mutation is audited, and connected stores re-synchronise nightly.
steps.why: Customers already keep secrets in an external store, here Google Cloud Secret Manager.
